issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

core

### Describe the bug

Request to /auth throws java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 0, Size: 0

### Version

23.0.6

### Expected behavior

No exception

### Actual behavior

I use the bitnami helm chart with `httpRelativePath: "/auth/"` which causes an exception when making requests to https://url/auth but no exception to https://url/auth/

### How to Reproduce?

Deploy keycloak with `httpRelativePath: "/auth/"` and make a request to url/auth

### Anything else?

Also documented here:  https://github.com/aerogear/keycloak-metrics-spi/issues/190

body: I could not reproduce this, so I am guessing that there is some additional complication that is causing the problem.
@geoand the missing piece should be the mixing of resteasy reactive and classic. When only classic is used that's a different context and UriInfo implementation.

Hm...

In that case I have no idea how we can solve it

> In that case I have no idea how we can solve it

It just seems to be a bug with the logic in resteasy reactive. The logic backing UriInfo.getMatchedURIs appears like it will always fail in the case when accessing the relative root - is that not generally possible? Could something like ResourceLocatorBaseResource / ResourceLocatorTest be modified to reproduce this?
If that's the case, then I don't see how it works for the cases I tried

@geoand had to delete my previous update - it was based upon an incorrect observation. I am able to reproduce this: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/compare/main...shawkins:quarkus:iss38663?expand=1 - if testRoot is run with -Dquarkus.http.root-path=/root you will see the index exception.
Thanks! I'll have a look later on today

Hm...

When I make the same change to `io.quarkus.resteasy.reactive.server.test.resource.basic.ResourceLocatorTest`  I don't see a failure
@geoand To clarify the issue is triggered by setting the root path. Are you not seeing an exception even when you specify something like quarkus.http.root-path=/foo

You are right, I had missed that!

Now I can reproduce it, but the problem is I have zero ideas on how to fix it, as I never understood the subresource crap in JAX-RS...

@geoand it could just be that this logic should not be allowed to return an empty string: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/8012cf53931cc02f4ba95eb78f4ec2e66143bbc2/independent-projects/resteasy-reactive/server/runtime/src/main/java/org/jboss/resteasy/reactive/server/core/ResteasyReactiveRequestContext.java#L438

It should likely return / instead of empty.
